title: Self-service service account request, attestation, and rotation workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As part of RBAC v2 and improved admin controls we need a safe, auditable self-service flow for creating and managing service accounts. Current workflows are ad-hoc (manual tickets + shared keys), causing over-privileged accounts, unclear ownership, and poor rotation practices. Scope: Implement a console-driven request + attestation UI, automated least-privilege policy generation via selectable templates, owner assignment, TTL-based credential issuance, and automated rotation/expiry. Integrate all events into our audit logging pipeline (SIEM) and surface critical signals in Console. Non-goals: Replacing Dedicated provisioning APIs or retrofitting existing long-lived service accounts created outside the system in first iteration.
proposed_solution: High-level flow: 1) Developer requests a new service account from Console -> selects intent category (e.g., data-pipeline, infra-agent, model-serving) which maps to a least-privilege template. 2) Attestation form requires a justification, list of repos/projects, and a named owner (SSO user or SSO group). 3) Approval rules: for low-privilege templates, auto-approve for certain SSO groups; for medium/high, route to manager + security reviewer. 4) On approval, system creates the SA in canonical registry, generates minimal IAM policy, tags the account, and issues short-lived credentials (JWT / ephemeral key with TTL). 5) Rotation: built-in lifecycle manager rotates keys automatically before TTL expiry and rotates every X days for long-lived delegations; policy enforces mandatory rotation or revocation. 6) Audit: all request/approval/credential events emitted to audit-log topic with structured fields (requester, owner, template, reason, TTL, approvers, git-PR links) and forwarded to SIEM + Console timeline. 7) API/CLI parity: expose request and rotation endpoints for infra automation. Implementation details: - Use least-privilege templates stored in config repo (yaml) with parameterized resources and example statements. - Policy generator will expand template with project identifiers and produce final policy vetted by a policy linter. - Ownership is required; service accounts with no owner become stale and enter a review/expiration cadence. - Enforce SSO group-based policies via SAML/SCIM sync to map approvers and auto-approval eligibility.
tradeoffs_decisions: Decisions made: - Ephemeral-first: issue short-lived credentials by default to reduce blast radius; long-lived credentials optional with explicit security review. - Template model vs freeform policy: templates reduce risk but may under-approximate needed permissions; we'll allow template extensions via a formal exception process. - Approval complexity: favor automation where possible (auto-approve for infra teams) to reduce friction; accept manual approvals for wide-scope templates. Trade-offs: - Developer friction vs security: TTL and attestation add onboarding cost; mitigated by providing SDK/CLI flows and templated common use-cases. - Work to onboard legacy accounts: we will run a migration campaign with discovery dashboards rather than immediate blocking, to avoid operational impact.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary - teams alpha): build Console request UI, template catalog, approval rules, and emit audit events to staging SIEM. Target teams: infra, model-serving. Duration 3 weeks. Phase 2 (broader rollout): add auto-rotation, CLI/API endpoints, and migration tooling to identify unmanaged SAs; expand auto-approve groups. Duration 4 weeks. Phase 3 (enforcement): after metrics and security review, require all new service accounts to be created via the flow and start expiration windows for legacy SAs. Phase 4: integrate with Dedicated/Private deployments to surface local SAs and mirror audit events. Each phase includes security review, design review, and a 1-week canary with detailed monitoring. Release gate: security-2026.03 with opt-in first, enforced in subsequent release.
monitoring_and_metrics: Key metrics to track: - % of service accounts created via self-service flow (goal >80% after phase 2) - Average time from request -> approval -> credential issuance (goal <30m for auto-approve) - Number of over-privilege exceptions granted - % of SAs with no owner (goal <5%) - Rotation completion rate and failed rotations - Number of audit log events ingested per day from SA flow Dashboards: create Console dashboard 'SA Lifecycle' showing counts by template, owner, stale accounts, rotation failures, and SIEM alerts. Add alerts for >1 failed rotation in 24h, unapproved long-lived SA creation, and spike in SA creation rate.
